newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end mixed, electronics rebound.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end mixed, electronics rebound.

text.p: Taiwan share prices closed mixed on Thursday as electronics rebounded strongly while investors actively sold financials and plastics, brokers said.
The index ended a scant 7.72 points or 0.09 percent lower at 8,259.28, well back from an opening high of 8,342.02.
Turnover was a modestly active T$121.6 billion.
Electronics, which suffered heavy profit-taking on Wednesday, rebounded 2.95 percent as leading chipmaker Taiwan Semiconductor rose the daily seven percent limit to T$91 on its ex-bonus issue date.
Chipmaker Mosel rose T$3 to T$74.5.
Brokers said a recent downward correction in electronics was due mainly to the fact that some electronics firms did not enjoy sound sales performance in May.

"Notebook computer and scanner makers may not be able to continue to enjoy high sales growth in the near future, but the upstream semiconductor and components makers have just started their recovery," said Taiwan International Securities assistant vice-president Alex Chiu.
Financials continued their recent weak performance, falling 1.77 percent, while plastics slid 0.75 percent.
Grand Petrochemical fell T$1 to T$29.
Brokers attributed the recent consolidation partly to tightening liquidity, especially after the central bank issued T$10 billion of negotiable certificates of deposit on Tuesday.
"The tightening liquidity did affect some buying momentum, but we could see active entries during recent index declines," said Golden Securities research chief Albert Lin.
China-concept shares -- Taiwan firms with active or planned investments in the communist mainland -- also rebounded, with shoemaker Pou Chen limit up to T$148.
Brokers said the consolidation would be short-lived, and they saw a firming trend ahead.
